name: TX-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Pfluger with large financial advantage ($2.9M cash vs $47K)
No polls or expert ratings; challenger is minimally funded
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~3%
model.rationale: Pfluger holds a deeply Republican seat, is running for reelection, and has out-raised Claire Reynolds by more than 35-to-1 with no outside opposition spending. Markets price a Democratic win at roughly 3%, consistent with the fundamentals-based margin near -18.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic outside spending or an unexpected incumbent scandal would be the main ways this moves toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Texas's 11th District is a solidly Republican seat, and two-term incumbent August Pfluger is seeking reelection after easily securing renomination. His campaign has raised about $3.2 million and holds $2.9 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Claire Reynolds has raised under $90,000 with minimal cash remaining and no outside support on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's R+17 lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and prediction markets that give Reynolds roughly a 3% chance. The expected margin is around 18 points Republican, with the race rated Safe R and high confidence in that assessment.
